text_en: The last naturally conceived Pyrenean ibex is found dead, presumed to have been killed by a falling tree.

In Soria (Spain) a large chunk of ice is reported to have fallen from the sky. Over the following months, a social panic about this phenomenon is unleashed, with reports of a multitude of similar cases of falling ice chunks (incorrectly named as aerolites) all over Spain, attracting great attention from the Spanish media.
America Online announces an agreement to purchase Time Warner for $162 billion (the largest-ever corporate merger).
Kenya Airways Flight 431 crashes off the Ivory Coast into the Atlantic Ocean, killing 169 people.
Alaska Airlines Flight 261 crashes off the California coast into the Pacific Ocean, killing all 88 passengers and crew.
Second Chechen War: Battle of Grozny (1999–2000) ends as Russian forces conclude capture of the Chechen capital Grozny.
Torrential rains in Africa led to the worst flooding in Mozambique in 50 years, which lasts until March and kills 800 people.
Final Peanuts comic is printed in newspapers, preceded by author Charles M. Schulz's death the night before. It is the most popular comic strip in history, running for 50 years.
Microsoft releases Windows 2000.
UNESCO holds the inaugural celebration of International Mother Language Day.

A rare century leap year date occurs. Usually, century years are common years due to not being exactly divisible by 400. 2000 is the first such year to have a February 29 since the year 1600, making it only the second such occasion since the Gregorian Calendar was introduced in 1582. The next such leap year will occur in 2400.
Sony releases the PlayStation 2 in Japan to compete with the Dreamcast. It launches in other countries later in the year.

The NASDAQ Composite Index reaches an all-time high of 5,048. Two weeks later, the NASDAQ-100, S&P 500, and Wilshire 5000 reach their peaks prior to the Dot-com bubble, ending a bull market run that had lasted over 17 years.
The United States dollar becomes the official currency of Ecuador, replacing the Ecuadorian sucre.
Uganda mass suicide: 778 members of the Movement for the Restoration of the Ten Commandments of God die in Uganda.
2000 Russian presidential election: Vladimir Putin is elected President of Russia.
Air Philippines Flight 541, a Boeing 737-200, crashes during approach at Davao City, Philippines, killing 131 people, making it the deadliest air disaster in the Philippines.
Canonization of Polish Catholic sister Faustina Kowalska in the presence of 200,000 people and the first Divine Mercy Sunday is celebrated worldwide.
A new class of composite material is fabricated, which has a combination of physical properties never before seen in a natural or human-made material.
The Selective Availability limiter is removed from the Global Positioning System, allowing for practical general-purpose use. The date is sometimes known as "Blue Switch Day".

The 7.6 .mw-parser-output .tooltip-dotted{border-bottom:1px dotted;cursor:help}Moment mag. scale</span>"}]]}'>Mw Central Sulawesi earthquake affects Banggai, Indonesia, with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VII (Very strong), leaving 46 dead and 264 injured.
India's population reaches 1 billion.
Real Madrid C.F. defeats Valencia CF 3–0 in the UEFA Champions League Final at Stade de France to win their second title between 1998 and 2002, and their eighth overall.
The 7.9 Mw Enggano earthquake shakes southwestern Sumatra, killing 103 people and injuring at least 2,174.
July 2 – Belgium and the Netherlands jointly host the UEFA Euro 2000 football tournament, which is won by France.
A centennial earthquake (6.5 on the Richter scale) hits Iceland on its national day.
Another earthquake hits Iceland further west than the previous quake.
A first draft of the Human Genome Project is finished. It is announced at the White House by U.S. President Clinton with Francis Collins and Craig Venter jointly with the UK Prime Minister in London.
The Øresund Bridge between Denmark and Sweden is officially opened for traffic.

France defeats Italy 2–1 after extra time in the final of the UEFA Euro 2000 Championship in Association football, becoming the first team to win the World Cup and European Championship consecutively.
Vicente Fox of the National Action Party (PAN) is elected President of Mexico, becoming the first president not from the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) since 1929.
In southern Nigeria, a leaking petroleum pipeline explodes, killing about 250 villagers who were scavenging gasoline.

25 – A summit meeting takes place at Camp David between United States president Bill Clinton, Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak and Palestinian Authority chairman Yasser Arafat, ending without an agreement.
A powerful solar flare, later named the Bastille Day event, causes a geomagnetic storm on Earth.
Air France Flight 4590, a Concorde aircraft, crashes into a hotel in Gonesse just after takeoff from Paris, killing all 109 aboard and 4 in the hotel.
The US Confederate submarine H. L. Hunley is raised to the surface after 136 years on the ocean floor.
The Russian submarine Kursk sinks in the Barents Sea during one of the largest Russian naval exercises since the 1991 dissolution of the Soviet Union, resulting in the deaths of all 118 men on board.
Tsar Nicholas II and his family are canonized by the synod of the Russian Orthodox Church.
The state funeral of Abulfaz Elchibey, the second President of Azerbaijan, takes place in Baku.
The Nokia 3310 mobile phone is released.
The last wholly Swedish-owned arms manufacturer, Bofors, is sold to American arms manufacturer United Defense.
8 – World leaders attend the Millennium Summit at U.N. Headquarters.
14 – Fuel protests in the United Kingdom, with refineries blockaded and supply to the country's network of petrol stations halted.
Steve Jobs introduces the Mac OS X Public Beta for US$29.95.
Microsoft releases Windows Me.
October 1 – The 2000 Summer Olympics, held in Sydney, Australia, is the first Olympic Games of the 2000s.
Ukrainian journalist Georgiy Gongadze is last seen alive; this day is taken as the commemoration date of his death.
The 2000 Xenia Tornado leaves 100 people injured, one person dead and 321+ houses destroyed.
The Greek ferry Express Samina sinks off the coast of the island of Paros; 80 out of a total of over 500 passengers perish in one of Greece's worst sea disasters.
Israeli opposition leader Ariel Sharon visits the Temple Mount in East Jerusalem, sparking an uprising that becomes the Second Intifada.
Approximate start of Autumn 2000 Western Europe floods (particularly affecting the UK), precipitated by days of heavy rain.
Mass demonstrations in Belgrade lead to resignation of Yugoslavia's president Slobodan Milošević.
250 million US gallons (950,000 m3) of coal sludge spill in Martin County, Kentucky, United States (considered a greater environmental disaster than the Exxon Valdez oil spill).

In Aden, Yemen, USS Cole is badly damaged by two Al-Qaeda suicide bombers, who place a small boat laden with explosives alongside the United States Navy destroyer, killing 17 crew members and wounding at least 39.
Hatfield rail crash: A Great North Eastern Railway Intercity 225 express train is derailed, killing four people and injuring many others, in Hatfield, Hertfordshire, England.

Pakistani authorities announce that their police have found an apparent mummy of an alleged Persian Princess in the province of Balochistan, Pakistan. The governments of Iran, Pakistan as well as the Taliban of Afghanistan all claim the mummy until Pakistan announces it is a modern-day forgery in April 2001.
Expedition 1 to the International Space Station begins.
2000 United States presidential election: No winner can be declared, prompting a controversial recount in Florida.
Kaprun disaster, Austria: A funicular fire in an Alpine tunnel kills 155 skiers and snowboarders.
The United States recognizes the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.
Bihar is divided into two parts (by the Bihar Reorganisation Act, 2000) and Jharkhand, the 28th state of India, is created. Hence, this day is celebrated as Jharkhand Foundation Day.

Alberto Fujimori, President of Peru, faxes his resignation from a hotel room in Japan, having fled Peru after facing corruption charges. Fujimori would be officially removed from office by Congress on the 22nd.
Kadisoka temple is discovered in Sleman, Yogyakarta, Indonesia.

Bush v. Gore: The United States Supreme Court rules that the recount of the 2000 presidential election in Florida should be halted and the original results be certified, thus making George W. Bush the winner of the U.S. presidential election.
The third and final reactor at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant is shut down and the station is shut down completely.
In the 2000 Serbian parliamentary election an alliance of reformist parties achieves a landslide victory over the nationalists, paving the way for a government under Zoran Đinđić.
The Christmas Eve bombings in several churches in Indonesia kill 18 people.
The Luoyang Christmas fire at a shopping center in China kills 309 people.
